paper_diagnosis: Pulmonary manifestation of Plasmodium falciparum malaria: case patient 2
disease_label_per_paper: P. falciparum malaria complicated by delayed post-treatment ARDS and AKI
presentation_summary: 23-year-old man presented with 5 days of fever, headache, anorexia, nausea, and vomiting.
Initial examination showed temperature 39.4 C, pulse 78/min, RR 20/min, BP 100/50 mmHg, and room-air oxygen saturation 100%.
Initial labs showed platelet count 21 x10^9/L, creatinine 163 micromol/L, urea 11 mmol/L, glucose 5 mmol/L, ALT 99 U/L, bilirubin 50 micromol/L, and albumin 26 g/L.
Initial CXR was normal and blood film confirmed P. falciparum with parasitemia 0.14%; he started oral artemether/lumefantrine and repeat smear became negative.

On hospital day 3 he developed cough, hemoptysis, breathlessness, RR 35/min, oxygen saturation 90-95% on 15 L non-rebreather mask, PaO2/FiO2 ratio 192, and bilateral CXR shadowing consistent with pulmonary edema or ARDS.
He moved to ICU for furosemide and BPAP support and improved with supportive treatment.
